description:
Found by the fz-kdt.127 research (2026-09-02, r3/report.md surprise 3).
body_consumes_callable_identity (jobs/keying.rs:257) is true when the body
has capture params, ANY ClosureCall tail, or ANY Lambda step -- whole-body
syntax, no flow, no per-slot view. List.reduce/3 keys precisely per
reducer only because its :suspend clause builds a thunk (list.fz:22-24);
its running :cont path only forwards the reducer. So the fz-6gb sharing
rule is decided by clauses that may never run, and a per-slot / per-clause
consumption fact would share more (proportional compilation) without
changing what direct dispatch buys. Characterize: how many precisely-keyed
bodies in the corpus are precise only through a non-running clause;
whether DispatchMask (jobs/keying.rs:451) already carries enough to make
consumption per slot. Sequence after fz-kdt.127.
title: consumes_callable_identity is syntactic: a body keys precisely for a clause it never runs
